title: Herschel Evans, Lester Young and Jack Washington
summary: Jones calls Herschel Evans the greatest musician he played with, says Lester stayed in the band with difficulty afterward, and praises Jack Washington.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: The greatest musicians that I ever played with in my life that gave me the feeling, was Herschel. Nobody, nobody. He lifted you out of your seat. He could do it with 8 bars. Don't ask me how he did it; you just floated. You floated, and everybody had this erroneous thing about Lester and Herschel. It was like hams and eggs and bacon and eggs. And it was very difficult to keep Lester in the band after he died. He was leaving every night and he had his coat and hat on the bandstand and Jack had to pull him down because Jack sat with him.
Jack Washington. That was the biggest thing in the Basie saxophone section. He was the king of all of them.
